root_cause_label: Wrong Python Environment Targeted — Installed Into Venv Instead of Patching System Fasttext
one_sentence_failure_summary: After observing that the OpenHands venv lacks access to system site-packages, the agent incorrectly concluded the fix was to install fasttext into the venv, never investigating the actual numpy 2.x API incompatibility in the system-wide fasttext installation that the benchmark's pytest runner uses.
t_err_evidence: pip install fasttext -> Requirement already satisfied: fasttext in /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages (wrong env, not venv)
t_commit_evidence: At step 7 the agent runs 'pip install fasttext' targeting the system environment (which already has it) and then at step 8 runs 'pip install --force-reinstall --no-cache-dir fasttext', committing entirely to reinstalling fasttext rather than patching the numpy incompatibility in FastText.py; no subsequent step pursues the correct fix.
t_surface_evidence: import fasttext -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fasttext' (still fails after install attempt)
trigger_explanation: The agent observed that the venv's sys.path excludes system site-packages and jumped to the conclusion that making fasttext importable inside the venv was the required fix. This false premise caused it to ignore the actual root cause: a numpy 2.x API change (np.array with copy=False -> np.asarray) in /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fasttext/FastText.py. The agent never tested the system python3 interpreter directly, never triggered the real AttributeError, and never realized the benchmark runs under system Python.
